tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description opens with imperative phrasing ('Use this skill for any investigation that involves AWS WAF...') and lists explicit trigger scenarios (403 Forbidden, CAPTCHA, false positive decisions, SQLi/XSS/traversal/Log4j, bot/credential stuffing, Count-to-Block, DDoS, IP lookup) that focus on what the user is trying to achieve, not internal mechanics. It is a single long sentence/paragraph but stays scoped to triggers and coverage, remaining reasonably concise while being appropriately pushy about scope.
tests.evidence: "Use this skill for any investigation that involves AWS WAF: a customer or partner getting 403 Forbidden, a CAPTCHA or a challenge page; deciding whether a block was a false positive; SQL injection, XSS, path traversal or Log4j attempts and whether anything got through; scrapers, bots or credential stuffing that WAF allowed; whether a rule running in Count mode can be switched to Block; traffic floods, DDoS events, Anti-DDoS rule group or rate-based rule behaviour; or who a specific client IP is."

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body avoids explaining general WAF/AWS concepts the agent would already know, and instead focuses on non-obvious, environment-specific facts (e.g., Athena workgroup constraints, label semantics, CloudFront metric dimension quirks). While dense, nearly every sentence conveys project-specific or domain-specific knowledge rather than generic background.
tests.evidence: "This skill adds WAF analysis method to an investigation. You already know how to query the data. What this skill adds is which questions to ask of it..."

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The body contains guidance and short rules but delegates detailed reference data (query environment specifics, log/metric facts, method-specific procedures) to separate reference files rather than embedding large tables or lookup data inline.
tests.evidence: "Read [query-environment.md](references/query-environment.md) first." and "Before your first log query, read [log-data-facts.md](references/log-data-facts.md)."

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: All nine files in references/ are linked via markdown links in the body.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link is tied to a specific triggering condition or question type, telling the agent exactly when to load it.
tests.evidence: "S3 bucket, or Firehose to S3: use Athena. Read [query-environment.md](references/query-environment.md) first." and the table mapping question types to reference files (e.g., '"My customer got blocked"... | [false-positive.md](references/false-positive.md) |')

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths rooted at references/ with no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile operations (Athena query constraints, rule change plans, CloudFront metric dimensions) are given exact prescriptive steps, while classification and attribution judgments (e.g., grouping by behavior) are described with reasoning and flexibility rather than rigid steps.
tests.evidence: "use a workgroup with Athena managed query results, never pass `ResultConfiguration`, run only SELECT" vs "Fingerprints find candidates; behaviour decides who is in a group. Compare when clients were active..."

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: The skill designates a clear default per situation (e.g., CloudWatch Logs Insights vs Athena based on log destination) rather than presenting multiple tools as equal options.
tests.evidence: "CloudWatch Logs log group: use Logs Insights. Nothing else is needed." / "S3 bucket, or Firehose to S3: use Athena."

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches generalizable investigation methods (how to pick an engine, how to attribute, how to conclude within evidence) applicable to any WAF investigation, not a one-off task declaration.
tests.evidence: "A broad \"what happened on this WebACL\" review usually needs several: start with metrics for the window, then the injection method for blocked traffic..."

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill is rich with concrete, non-obvious gotchas woven through Step 3 and elsewhere (e.g., label semantics, JA4 fingerprint pitfalls, metric dimension traps), satisfying the gotchas requirement even without a dedicated section title.
tests.evidence: "A shared User-Agent is weak evidence. A shared JA4 means a shared TLS library, not a shared operator." and "a query with it returns no datapoints."

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill provides an explicit output structure for findings/conclusions (the Step 4 wording table and investigation structure guidance) appropriate to its reporting purpose.
tests.evidence: "| Situation | Strongest wording |\n|---|---|\n| Blocked request that looks legitimate | \"WAF-side likely false-positive candidate, needs business confirmation\" |"

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The only table-like structure in the body (Step 4 wording table) is short, well under 20 lines, so no large inline template needing extraction to assets/ exists.
tests.evidence: "| Situation | Strongest wording |\n|---|---|\n| Blocked request that looks legitimate | ... |"
